newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: FORECAST - MAS half-year net seen flat.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - MAS half-year net seen flat.

text.p: High fuel costs and an ambitious fleet expansion plan are expected to stunt the half-year earnings of national carrier Malaysian Airline System Bhd (MAS), equity analysts said on Tuesday.

The airline was expected to report flat net earnings for the six months to September 30, 1996, of around 140 million ringgit ($55.3 million), against 139.5 million in the same period a year ago, they said.
Profits are also likely to remain under pressure for the full year to March 31, 1997, the analysts said.
"There's nothing to look forward to in the short-term... the second half will be much worse because high fuel costs are still there," said Tan Geok Hock, airline analyst at Schroder Research.
MAS is expected to report its half-year results after 0930 GMT on Tuesday, a company official said.

In late October, a spokesman for the International Air Transport Asociation (IATA) said the average worldwide price of fuel paid by IATA members during the first nine months of this year was 73 U.S. cents per US gallon, against 65 cents in 1995, an increase of 13.3 percent.
With fuel costs -- which comprise roughly 15 percent of MAS's total expenditures -- forecast to remain high in the next few months, MAS margins will continue to be pressured, analysts said.
"Fuel costs will continue to rise (for the rest of the year) but not as steeply," said Choo Swee Kee, transport analyst at Vickers Ballas Research.
MAS has embarked on a large-scale fleet expansion, which would keep investors wary of the stock because they might have to ultimately pay for the new aircraft, analysts said.
Analysts said another private placement of shares or a rights issue in the near future would not please investors as earnings per share would be diluted.
"Shareholders will not be too happy with another cash call," said an analyst at a unit trust fund.
The airline announced in January it was buying 25 Boeing passenger jets over the next five years for 10 billion ringgit (US$3.9 billion).
The company in May raised 500 million ringgit from a private placement of 10 percent of its share capital at the time, or 70 million shares, to institutional investors.
The Estimate Directory of consensus analyst forecasts puts MAS net earnings for the year ended March 31, 1997, at 306 million ringgit, against 232.9 million ringgit in the year to March 31, 1996.
At 0700 GMT, MAS stock was up 15 cents to 6.55 ringgit.
